Subject: PrivCP identity mesh bootstrap & JIT entitlement model — kickoff and questions

Hi team,

Thanks for agreeing to a short kickoff on the private control plane identity integration. Attached is a compact proposal that sketches an "identity mesh" approach and a just-in-time (JIT) entitlement path for operator/admin access in VPC/on-prem deployments. High-level goals:

- Minimize long-lived privileged service accounts inside customer VPCs.
- Allow customer IdP to control entitlements via SCIM group deltas with an auditable token-exchange path.
- Preserve emergency operator access with a documented break-glass flow.

Requests before our technical sync on Wednesday:
1) Can you share an authoritative SAML metadata URL and one sample SP-initiated SAML assertion we can test in staging?
2) For SCIM: do you support incremental delta sync and granular group attributes (role, ttl_seconds)?
3) Any compliance constraints (IP allowlists, cert pinning) for the control plane egress we should account for?

Attachment: identity-mesh-proposal.pdf (6 pages — architecture diagram, token flow, SCIM mapping table).

I cc'd Dylan and Rishi — Dylan please flag any runtime implications (service account lifecycle, token cache) and Rishi please note compliance points. Mina: can you own the runbook draft after the sync?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa and team,

Thanks for the proposal — this direction looks promising. Quick answers to your questions:

1) SAML metadata: https://idp.acme.com/saml/metadata.xml (we'll provide a signed copy in the sync).
2) SCIM: our IdP supports SCIM 2.0 and incremental change tokens (we expose /scim/v2/Users and /Groups with startIndex/Resources for deltas). We can include a custom attribute "redwood_role" on Group membership entries; TTL is not natively in our group model, but we can set an extension attribute ttlSeconds.
3) Compliance constraints: outbound to your control-plane endpoints must be from the corporate egress IPs we provide; mutual TLS for provisioning endpoints is preferred.

Attached is a sample metadata export and an anonymized delta payload for a recent group change.

Next steps: we'll be on the call Wednesday at 14:00 PST. I'll hand the meeting to our infra lead for the SAML exchange demo.

Best,

Subject: Re: PrivCP identity mesh bootstrap & JIT entitlement model — kickoff and questions

Thanks Marcus — that SCIM delta example helps a lot. A few notes to shape the technical agenda:

- Token exchange model: we propose short-lived operator tokens minted by the private control plane after validating SCIM group assertions and a SAML assertion for the initiating operator. The tokens are scoped (role, resource, ttl) and stored only in volatile KV in the control plane — no long-lived key persisted in the host.

- Service account lifecycle: where we need long-lived credentials (e.g., for monitoring agents), we want to use a platform-managed service account with narrow scopes and rotate it via the platform KMS. For customer-managed service accounts, we'll accept public keys and record key fingerprints in the provisioning manifest.

- Just-in-time entitlements: we can support an on-demand mapping that creates ephemeral roles based on SCIM group attributes. Need to confirm whether Acme can provide the "redwood_role" attribute and if they can include expiration/ttlSeconds in the delta payload.

- Edge-case: offline operator access. We propose a break-glass artifact (time-limited single-use signed URL or a one-time OTP flow) logged to audit with approval metadata. This requires an emergency operator journey in the runbook.

I'm attaching a short checklist of runtime checks I want to run in staging (token validation, clock skew tolerance, SCIM delta replay, mTLS handshake).

-Dylan
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Quick alignment notes post-sync:

- Compliance: Acme's egress IPs + mTLS requirement is acceptable. We should capture the IP list and cert fingerprints in the contract addendum and in the platform allowlist. Mina, please draft the compliance appendix.

- Audit: every JIT token mint must emit a single-line audit entry with operator id, role, resource, ttl, and request origin (SAML assertion id + SCIM delta id). These need to be exportable to our SIEM in near-real time.

- Failure modes: define a clear fallback to a customer-approved emergency operator (with human approval) if SCIM delta processing fails for > 5 minutes. Also define how we invalidate tokens if SCIM indicates a revocation.

- Testing: Dylan, lead the staging checklist and include SCIM replay (old deltas), clock skew tests (+/- 2 minutes), and SAML replay protections.

I'll prepare a short compliance acceptance criteria doc and share by Monday.

-Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
